newsitem.title: USA: Barnett net income falls after charge.
newsitem.headline: Barnett net income falls after charge.

text.p: Barnett Banks, Inc., the largest banking company in Florida, Wednesday posted weaker quarterly profits after taking a $15.3 million charge for a special fee to recapitalize the federal bank insurance fund.
Net income fell to $127.0 million, or 65 cents a share, in the third quarter from $134.1 million, or 65 cents a share, in the year-ago period.

The results include an after-tax charge of 8 cents a share for the special assessment to inject new capital into the Savings Association Insurance Fund as a result of legislation signed into law on Sept. 30.
Barnett, one of the nation's top 25 banks, said its operating profits continued to grow, with the quarter's return on average assets rising to 1.4 percent from 1.3 percent in the year-ago period.

"We continue to realise the earning power of our franchise," said Charles E. Rice, Barnett chairman and chief executive. "Our profitability continues to increase as we optimize our business lines and develop new sources of profitable revenue."
Net interest income increased 5 percent to $469.0 million, after the Jacksonville, Fla.-based company changed the mix of earning assets and lowered funding costs.
Non-interest income rose 7 percent to $194.9 million, while consumer finance income jumped more than 30 percent, it said.
Barnett's stock fell 62.5 cents to $35.375 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
